articles.title: USN-9068-1: Debian-LAN vulnerability
articles.summary: Wolfgang Schweer discovered that Debian-LAN configured overly permissive ACLs for the Kerberos admin server. An authenticated user could possibly use this issue to change the credentials of other users, leading to privilege escalation.

articles.title: USN-9089-1: x11vnc vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that x11vnc created shared memory segments with insecure permissions. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain sensitive information or modify screen contents.

articles.title: USN-9088-1: TigerVNC vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that the TigerVNC viewer stored TLS certificate exceptions as trusted certificate authorities. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to impersonate any VNC server after a user had added a certificate exception for the attacker's server.

articles.title: USN-9087-1: signing-party vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that the gpg-key2ps tool in signing-party did not properly sanitize user IDs before passing them to a shell. If a user were tricked into processing a specially crafted OpenPGP key, an attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary commands.

articles.title: USN-9086-1: SA-Exim vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that SA-Exim unsafely evaluated the parameters of its greylisting SpamAssassin rule. An attacker able to write SpamAssassin configuration files or rules could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary code.

articles.title: USN-9085-1: Ruby OpenID vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that Ruby OpenID sent a request to the claimed identifier URL before verifying the signature of an OpenID response. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to perform server-side request forgery attacks.

articles.title: USN-9084-1: Radicale vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that Radicale did not delay failed authentication attempts when using htpasswd authentication. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain user passwords through timing or brute-force attacks.

articles.title: USN-9083-1: gevent vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that the gevent WSGI server incorrectly validated chunked transfer encoding trailers in HTTP requests. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to perform HTTP request smuggling attacks, leading to privilege escalation.

articles.title: USN-9082-1: pngquant vulnerability
articles.summary: Choi Jaeseung discovered that pngquant incorrectly handled certain PNG images, leading to a buffer overflow. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause pngquant to crash or execute arbitrary code.

articles.title: USN-9063-1: Yodl vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that Yodl incorrectly handled certain input, leading to a buffer over-read. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause Yodl to crash, resulting in a denial of service.

articles.title: USN-9062-1: SNMPTT vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that SNMPTT did not properly sanitize trap data passed to commands run through the EXEC, PREEXEC, and unknown_trap_exec options. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary shell commands.

articles.title: USN-9060-1: kramdown vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that kramdown processed the template option in documents by default. An attacker could possibly use this issue to read arbitrary files or execute arbitrary code.

articles.title: USN-9059-1: ruby-jwt vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that ruby-jwt incorrectly verified HMAC signatures when the verification key was empty or missing. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to forge tokens and bypass authentication.

articles.title: USN-9058-1: Action Pack Page Caching vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that Action Pack Page Caching incorrectly handled certain request paths when writing cached pages. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to write arbitrary files to the web server, and possibly execute arbitrary code.

articles.title: USN-9057-1: rkhunter vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that rkhunter downloaded mirror updates over an insecure channel. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary code.

articles.title: USN-9056-1: Prosody Community Modules vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that the LDAP authentication modules in Prosody Community Modules did not fully verify XMPP addresses when checking for administrator privileges. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to gain administrator privileges.

articles.title: USN-9055-1: pecl_http vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that pecl_http incorrectly handled certain HTTP request parameters, leading to a type confusion. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to cause PHP to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or execute arbitrary code.

articles.title: USN-9054-1: Babel vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that Babel incorrectly evaluated certain code during compilation when used with certain plugins. If a user or an automated system were tricked into compiling specially crafted code, an attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary code.

articles.title: USN-9053-1: NetworkManager-ssh vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that NetworkManager-ssh did not properly validate extra options in VPN connection settings. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to escalate privileges.

articles.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
articles.summary: The cybercrime group Qilin has emerged as the world's most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months alone. But even top Russian hackers make operational security mistakes, and the administrator of Qilin has made a few key missteps over the last decade that all point to a 36-year-old man living in St. Petersburg, Russia.

articles.title: USN-9001-1: ca-certificates update
articles.summary: It was discovered that the ca-certificates JKS integration was not working properly, resulting in CA certificates removed from the system bundle not being removed from the JKS keystore. This update corrects the feature and resyncs the keystore with the system CA certificates list.

articles.title: USN-8994-1: libvips vulnerabilities
articles.summary: It was discovered that libvips incorrectly handled certain PDF files with a page that defines a width but not a height. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause libvips to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or obtain sensitive information. This issue only affected Ubuntu 16.04 LTS, Ubuntu 18.04 LTS, Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. (CVE-2025-59933) It was discovered that libvips incorrectly determined image dimensions in the vipsload operation, leading to an integer overflow. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause libvips to crash, resulting...

articles.title: USN-8993-1: SOGo vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that SOGo used the client-supplied Origin header when constructing password reset links. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain password reset tokens and take over user accounts.

articles.title: USN-8992-1: Shapelib vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that the shpsort utility in Shapelib incorrectly handled certain inputs, leading to a double free. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service, or possibly execute arbitrary code.

articles.title: USN-8991-1: rxvt-unicode vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that rxvt-unicode incorrectly handled certain escape sequences. An attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary code if a user displayed specially crafted text in the terminal.

articles.title: USN-8990-1: Sprockets vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that Sprockets incorrectly handled certain specially crafted requests when the Sprockets server was used in production. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to access files outside of the application's root directory.

articles.title: USN-8988-1: Relax-and-Recover vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that Relax-and-Recover created a world-readable initrd when GRUB_RESCUE was enabled. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain sensitive information.

articles.title: USN-8987-1: libuser vulnerabilities
articles.summary: It was discovered that libuser did not properly validate the GECOS field when changing user information. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to corrupt the passwd file, resulting in a denial of service. (CVE-2015-3245) It was discovered that libuser modified the passwd file in place when updating user information. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to cause an inconsistent file state, resulting in a denial of service, or possibly escalate privileges. (CVE-2015-3246)

articles.title: USN-8986-1: Swift Mailer vulnerability
articles.summary: Dawid Golunski discovered that Swift Mailer did not properly sanitize e-mail addresses in the mail transport. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to pass extra parameters to the mail command and execute arbitrary code.

articles.title: USN-8985-1: Net::EasyTCP vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that Net::EasyTCP used the built-in Perl rand() function to generate encryption keys when no strong randomization module was present. An attacker could possibly use this issue to predict the keys and obtain sensitive information.

articles.title: USN-8984-1: jabberd2 vulnerability
articles.summary: It was discovered that jabberd2 allowed SASL ANONYMOUS authentication even when it was not enabled in the configuration. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to bypass authentication.
